Great question — here's exactly how it works right now and what the options are:

---

## How Saving Works Currently

The webapp **already auto-saves everything Marc does** — every checkbox, date change, frequency selection, note, and custom report he adds — directly to his **browser's localStorage**. So if Marc opens the site on his computer and makes changes, those changes persist every time he comes back **on that same browser/device**.

**However**, localStorage is device-specific. That means:
- If you open the site on your computer, you see your version
- If Marc opens it on his computer, he sees his version
- Changes made on one device do **not** sync to the other

---

## To Make Changes Truly Shared & Synced

For both of you to see the same live data in real time, I'd need to upgrade the app to use a **database backend**. That would mean:

| Feature | Current (localStorage) | With Database Upgrade |
|---|---|---|
| Marc's changes saved | ✅ On his device | ✅ Everywhere |
| Your changes visible to Marc | ❌ No | ✅ Yes |
| Changes survive clearing browser | ❌ No | ✅ Yes |
| Real-time sync across devices | ❌ No | ✅ Yes |

The upgrade is straightforward — I'd add a database so every save writes to a shared record, and anyone with the link always sees the latest version.

**Would you like me to do that upgrade?** It would make Marc's edits permanent and visible to you as well, no matter who makes changes or what device they're on.
